title: The Kav from the reshimu: not an opposite but a source, and the line that only measures
overview:
After the *tzimtzum* and the *reshimu*, the chapter turns to the *Kav*, the line drawn from the *reshimu*. It looks like its very opposite: the *reshimu* is a point that does not spread at all, and the whole thing of a line is spreading, up and down. But a line is made of points. The point is the *hiyuli* of the line, and like every *hiyuli*, a talent or the soul's power of movement, it does not spread because it is above spreading, not because it cannot. Like a student swallowing his Rebbe's words, it holds the whole Essence, and from it comes all the spreading.

The first line, the *kav katzar*, is still part of the *Ein Sof*, *stima d'chol stimin*. It is the *kav hamida*, the line of measure: a teacher hired before he knows his student, a yardstick that measures a house, the moon or the distance back up to the Essence. It makes only an above and a below. It includes everything in the point, from the power before the *tzimtzum*, but comes to the measure of the receivers, and so it is the *hiyuli* of every light they will receive.

sections.title: The question: the Kav looks like the very opposite of the reshimu
sections.summary: The *reshimu* is a point: everything withdrawn, nothing spreading down, no length and no breadth. Being only a point could even be a source of revelation; but having no spreading at all looks like a real *tzimtzum*. So how does the *Kav*, which is all spreading, come out of it?

phrases.he: (יד) ומעתה יש להבין בבחינת הקו והחוט שנמשך מבחינת הרשימו הנזכר לעיל, דרך פרט
ותחלה יש להבין בו בענין כללותו,
שהוא בחינת ההיפוך ממש מבחינת הרשימו הנזכר לעיל
כי הנה הנקודה מורה ההעלם והסתלקות הכל,
עד שלא נשאר רק כנקודה א'
וגם נקודה או רושם זה מורה בחינת העדר ההתפשטות למטה דוקא
דהיינו ענין העדר ההמשכה וההתגלות לאורך ורוחב
כצורת הי' שאין בו תוך וחלל כו' כידוע.

blocks.text: Chapter 14. The *inyan* (matter) of the *Or Ein Sof*, the *tzimtzum* (contraction) and the *reshimu* (impression) is finished, and now begins the *Kav v'chut*, the line and the thread.

phrases.he: והנה בענין צמצום שלו מלמעלה,
דהיינו מה שנשאר בבחינת נקודה לבד,
יוכל להיות שיהיה מזה להיפוך
phrases.en: It could be that really it could be the opposite from this.

phrases.he: מפני שמחמת זה יוכלל בו הכל בקיצור ורמז וכהאי גוונא
ואדרבה
phrases.en: just opposite

phrases.he: זהו עיקר סיבת כל גלוי ההשפעה כנזכר לעיל

blocks.text: It could be that really it could be the opposite from this. *V'adraba*, just the opposite.

phrases.he: אבל מה שמנקודה זו מורה העדר ההתפשטות לגמרי למטה לכאורה, זהו ודאי נקרא צמצום גמור ואמיתי
phrases.en: So it appears that the fact that the *reshimu* is totally into itself, and really the *reshimu* does not spread, so it would seem it's a real *tzimtzum*.

phrases.he: להעלים ולהסתיר לבלתי יבוא האור למטה
ואם כן איך יומשך מנקודה זו
היפוכו ממש,
phrases.en: *mamash* opposite

phrases.he: שהוא בחינת המשכה והתפשטות דקו כו'.

blocks.text:
The *tzimtzum* here means *kipshuto* (literally). So it appears that the *reshimu* is totally into itself and really does not spread, so it would seem to be a real *tzimtzum*.

*Mamash* opposite: the whole thing of the *Kav* is the *inyan* of *hispashtus* (spreading out). As it says in various places in Kabbala, the whole thing of the line is that it goes up and down: spreading is the main *inyan* of the *Kav*.

sections.title: Point and line are not opposites: the point is the hiyuli of the line
sections.summary: A line comes out of a point and is made of points. The point does not spread, but like every *hiyuli* that is not because it cannot: it is still above spreading, and all the spreading comes from it, as movement comes from the soul.

phrases.he: אך הנה ידוע שבאמת הנקודה והקו אינם ב' הפכים,
שהרי הקו נמשך מן הנקודה,
phrases.en: since the *Kav* actually comes out from the *nekuda*

phrases.he: ומחיבור נקודות יחד נעשה קו כו'.

blocks.text: In truth they are not really two opposites, since the *Kav* actually comes out from the *nekuda*. Here he is bringing geometry. The point, the line, the *shetach* (area), length and breadth, all these things are basically geometric *meshalim* (analogies).

This is like what the Hermetics have, and some of those things: what they call mystical geometry, and all kinds of crazy *meshugaas*. But don't forget *gematria*: *gematria* basically means geometry. Or rather, *gematria* really does not come from geometry; geometry comes from *gematria*.

sensitivity.reason: Dismisses the Hermetic tradition's mystical geometry as "crazy meshugaas".
sensitivity.publishable: Others too speak of a mystical geometry. But don't forget *gematria*: *gematria* basically means geometry. Or rather, *gematria* really does not come from geometry; geometry comes from *gematria*.

blocks.text: The real, upper geometry is this: the real *inyan* of a *nekuda* is not *davka* a shape. The whole *inyan* of a point is that it is *bilti mispashet*, it does not spread. Still, from the geometrical shapes downstairs, a circle with a line coming down and all that business, you can get something: they represent an upper thing, like a *mashal*.

blocks.title: A line is the distance between two dots
blocks.text: One of the things the dots downstairs show is that a line is made out of dots. As a matter of fact, in geometry the whole definition of a line is the shortest distance between two dots. A dot represents a position, and the whole thing about a position is that that's the position, *davka* that one: it does not spread. And a line is *davka* the distance between two positions, from one position to another. So we see that even in physical geometry a line is made up of dots.

phrases.he: אך הענין הוא כידוע
שהנקודה הוא כמו בחינת ההיולי לגבי הקו
וכמו כל בחינת היולי או חומר פשוט
שאף על פי שהוא בהעדר ההתפשטות דוקא,
אין זה הכרחי כלל,
phrases.en: doesn't mean it cannot be *mispashet*

phrases.he: רק מצד עצם מהות ההיולי,
phrases.en: just because of the fact that it's a *hiyuli*

phrases.he: מפני שהוא למעלה עדיין מבחינת התפשטות
phrases.en: it still remains higher than the *hispashtus*, really

phrases.he: ולזאת לא ירד מעצמותו

blocks.text: A *nekuda* is not opposite from a *Kav* in the sense of being an antagonistic opposition to it, but rather in the fact that it is a *hiyuli*.

blocks.title: The songwriter's talent
blocks.text: The whole thing of a *hiyuli*, as was learned in the previous chapters with a talent or with the *koach hatnua* (the power of movement), is that it is really not spread into the actual thing. The talent itself does not spread, and that is why it stays the same as it was before. A guy wrote a song; his talent did not decrease. And not only that: you can see the talent from the song. You say, "Wow, this guy is really talented." But really the talent didn't go into the song. The talent is a thing inside of itself.

That is the general thing of a *hiyuli*: it is not spread, and nonetheless the spreading comes *davka* from the *hiyuli*. Like the *koach hatnua*, and like the fact that dead dogs don't bark: the soul doesn't really go into the movement, and yet the movement spreads from the soul, to the point that it is a sign of it.

blocks.title: Even a chicken can understand this
blocks.text:
You can see it by the fact that a thing is just lying there, and this is something even a chicken can understand. As we say, *hanosen lasechvi vina*, "Who gives the rooster understanding": a chicken has a certain amount of understanding. It can tell between day and night; it can make the distinction. How do you know a chicken can understand this? Because that's how a vulture can tell: a vulture tells life from death by movement, and a vulture is a kind of bird, with about the same brain as a chicken.

You don't need to be a genius. A lot of these things here you really don't need to be such a genius to understand; it's just that nobody ever pointed it out to anybody: "Oh, hey, look at this." Even a chicken can understand that the spreading comes from the *etzem* (the essence), and that the spreading of the *koach hatnua* shows that the thing is alive.

And yet the soul itself is really a thing in itself. Every *hiyuli* or simple matter, though it is without spreading, it doesn't mean it cannot spread. It is just because it is a *hiyuli*. Not because it cannot spread: just the opposite, the whole spreading does come from it. But the thing itself is a *hiyuli*, which even when there is spreading still remains higher than the spreading.

phrases.he: וכמו היולי של חיות החי בגלוי,
בעודנה כלולה בעצם,
phrases.en: while it's still included in the *etzem*

phrases.he: שאינה מתפשטת להחיות כו'
וכהיולי של כח התנועה בעצם,
טרם שמתפשט להניע
וככח הצמיחה טרם שמתפשט להצמיח
וככח השכל טרם שמתפשט להשכיל,
וכהאי גוונא רבים בדומה
phrases.en: There's many many *meshalim* that you can say for this.

phrases.he: הרי יובן שהעדר ההתפשטות הזאת לא נקרא צמצום אמיתי מצד עצמו
אדרבה
phrases.en: just the opposite

phrases.he: הרי הוא כח ההיולי העצמי שממנו נמצא הכל בהתגלות והתפשטות
phrases.en: It's *davka* from this is what the *hispashtus* is coming from.

blocks.text: As was said, even a chicken can understand this, while it is still included in the *etzem*. There are many, many *meshalim* you can say for this.
It's not that it is actually a lack of ability to spread. *Adraba*, just the opposite: it is *davka* from this that the spreading is coming. As was said, a chicken can understand this.

sections.title: So is the reshimu: the student who swallows his teacher's words
sections.summary: The point does not spread because the whole Essence is gathered into it, not because it is cut off. Like a student absorbed in his Rebbe: while he listens he gives nothing out, and afterwards everything he gives out comes from that listening. So the *reshimu* is the source of the *Kav*.

phrases.he: וכהאי גוונא יובן
phrases.en: so in the same way it'll be understood

phrases.he: בבחינת נקודה לגבי הקו
phrases.en: the *reshimu* in relationship to the *Kav*

phrases.he: שהעדר התפשטותה הוא רק מצד היותה
בבחינת העצמיות שלמעלה מבחינת ההתפשטות עדיין
והגם שבאה על ידי צמצום הכל,
phrases.en: even though it comes from a *tzimtzum*

phrases.he: עד שלא נשאר רק כנקודה א' כנזכר לעיל,
אך הרי זה עצמו מורה שכל בחינת העצמיות כלול בה
phrases.en: that the whole *Atzmus* is included in the *reshimu*

phrases.he: ולהיות כן, בלתי מתפשטת למטה
phrases.en: that really does not: it didn't go out of *Ein Sof* at all

blocks.text: So in the same way it will be understood of the *reshimu* in relationship to the *Kav*.

It doesn't matter that it comes from a *tzimtzum*. As was explained, like the Gemara in the Mishna, the whole *Atzmus* (Essence) is included in the *reshimu*. And since the *reshimu* is really a point of the essence, even though it is after the *tzimtzum* it is still part of the *etzem*: the *etzem* contracted itself into a point. There is no spreading to the outside yet. The *reshimu* did not go outside of the *Ein Sof* yet; it's the line that goes outside. It does not spread down: it didn't go out of the *Ein Sof* at all.

And here is a very good *mashal* for this.

phrases.he: וכמשל התלמיד לפני רבו
דאיידי דטריד למבלע
phrases.en: he is very busy with swallowing, in other words, with absorbing what the Rebbe is saying

phrases.he: ונעשה כנקודה בצמצום כל עצמותו כו',
phrases.en: and his whole *Atzmus* is like gone there and he's becoming a whole *nekuda*

phrases.he: לא פליט להשפיע לזולתו בהתפשטות
אמנם אחר קבלתו,
phrases.en: but after he received

phrases.he: אדרבה
phrases.en: just the opposite

phrases.he: מזה הצמצום שהיה בבחינת נקודה, הוא שנמשך ממנו כל ההשפעה והתפשטות לזולתו כו'
phrases.en: from this itself came the whole *hashpa'a* and *hispashtus* to downstairs

phrases.he: וכמו שכתוב במקום אחר

blocks.title: The student swallowing his teacher's words
blocks.text: He is very busy swallowing, absorbing what the Rebbe is saying. You try to talk to him; he will not talk to you.

blocks.title: Reb Yoel Kahan listening to the Rebbe
blocks.text: Like Reb Yoel Kahan, for instance. When the Rebbe was talking, he would be totally entranced, listening to the Rebbe. "The *chozer* (the one who repeated the Rebbe's talks)?" a student asks. Right, right.

Or in general, a student listening to a Rebbe: his whole *Atzmus* is gone there, and he becomes a whole *nekuda*. This is the whole *inyan* of *daas* (knowledge, the mind's taking in of a thing). If the next guy asks him what the Rebbe is saying, they'll just shove him away: get out of here. He won't even say get out of here; he won't even hear him. He's so busy listening to the Rebbe.

But after he has received, *adraba*, just the opposite. That's why he can *chazer* (repeat) the whole thing by heart. And not just repeating it by heart: understanding it and giving an explanation to another guy works exactly the same way.

When his teacher was there he listened to him so well that he *mamash* had nothing to do with anything outside of this. His whole being was contracted away, and he was totally a point of just listening to his teacher. Not only was that not a *tzimtzum*: *adraba*, from this itself came the whole giving and spreading downstairs.

phrases.he: ומכל זה יובן שהקו הנמשך מן הנקודה
הוא רק כמו בחינת התפשטות מן היולי העצמי

blocks.text: It is not an opposite. It is a source: the *reshimu* is actually the source of the line. That they show opposite *inyanim* doesn't mean they are actually opposites. *Adraba*: that the point does not spread is what gives it the power for the spreading of the *Kav*, because that is why it absorbs into itself the whole entire *Ein Sof*, like the student absorbing from the Rebbe. So that's one *inyan*: it's not two opposites really.

sections.title: The short line: the Kav itself, still "the most hidden of all hidden"
sections.summary: The first *Kav*, the *kav katzar*, is the *Kav* itself: it barely comes out before it turns into the *machshava kduma*, and it is still part of the *Ein Sof*, no lesser than the *reshimu*. As the point is the *hiyuli* of the line, the line is the *hiyuli* of breadth and area.

phrases.he: אמנם מה שנמשך בבחינת קו קצר,
phrases.en: this thing that it is coming out in a way of a *kav katzar*

phrases.he: הנה מבואר במקום אחר,
שכמו שהנקודה בחינת היולי לגבי הקו,
כך הקו בחינת היולי לבחינת אורך ורוחב דשטח
phrases.en: A *Kav* is like a *hiyuli* to an area, a plane.

blocks.text:
*Amnam*, now the next thing: what is drawn as a short line, this thing that comes out in a way of a *kav katzar*. There are several *inyanim* in the *Kav*. In some places he calls it a *kav katzar* (a short line), and later on you will see him say it is even before the *tehiru tata'a* (the lower purity). It is still called *stima d'chol stimin* (the most hidden of all hidden), and it really is also part of the *Ein Sof*, even though it is after the *tzimtzum*, just as the *reshimu* is.

Not only that: it is not a lesser thing than the *reshimu*, in the same way that the *reshimu* is not a lesser thing than the *Or Ein Sof*. They are different powers. It is exactly the same as the *reshimu*, except that it is coming down. And it is not just that: this is about the level of power that it is, and it is not a lower level of power.
blocks.outOfPlace: The class starts line 33 at the end of side 1 (w3679, "amnam, ma shenimshach bivchinas kav katzar") before the alignment's mark for it on side 2.

blocks.text: In this explanation (sometimes it is explained backwards) the *Or Ein Sof* is basically *chesed* of the *Ein Sof*: the power of spreading is *chesed*. The *tzimtzum* and the *reshimu* are *gevura* of the *Ein Sof*. And the *Kav* is basically *tiferes* of the *Ein Sof*, which combines the two powers. *Chesed* means infinite *chesed* without any *tzimtzum* to it; the *tzimtzum* means an infinite *tzimtzum* without any spreading to it; and *tiferes* is the combination of the two.
blocks.outOfPlace: End of side 1, on the short line of line 33, which side 2 then rereads.

blocks.text: This *kav katzar* is the *etzem hakav*, the *Kav* itself, and it is called *stima d'chol stimin*. In other places it says of *stima d'chol stimin*: *leis machshava tfisa bei klal*, no thought grasps Him at all. Even the thought of *Adam Kadmon* cannot grasp it: not just the *chachma* and *bina* of *Adam Kadmon* but even its *Keser*, which is the *machshava kduma* (the primordial thought). This *kav katzar* is still called *stima d'chol stimin*, and it is still considered *bei*, "Him": still part of the "Him" that no thought grasps.
blocks.outOfPlace: Side 2 opens by resuming the short line of line 33, a few minutes before it rereads the line.

blocks.text:
In other places, in Kabbala and *Chassidus*, you'll see that when they refer to the *Kav* they are talking about *Adam Kadmon*. But that's the further extension. That's not this *kav hamida* (the line of measure), I don't think.

"Okay, but sometimes that's what it refers to." It's not the same thing. "The *kav hamida*? What do you mean? I think when it says that *Adam Kadmon* is *Kav*, it's because it's the *Kav v'chut* that goes into the..." Yeah. Whatever, but the basic thing is that it's not that *kav hamida* before *Adam Kadmon*.

But still, nonetheless, sometimes when it says the *Kav* it means *Adam Kadmon*. Other places say the *Kav* goes to the end of *Atzilus*. And just recently the class spoke of the whole *hishtalshelus* (chain of descent) of the *Kav v'chut*: the *Kav v'chut* goes all the way down to here. These are different *inyanim* in the *Kav*.

The *kav katzar* is the actual *etzem* of the *Kav*: it just comes out. It doesn't even reach *Adam Kadmon*. It just comes out, and immediately it turns into a circle, into the *hiyuli d'tehiru* (the *hiyuli* of the space), which is the *machshava kduma*. That is the *Kav*; that is the *kav katzar*.
A *Kav* is like a *hiyuli* to an area, a plane. In the same way that you make a line by having a point travel between two other points, you make an area by having a line travel between two lines.

sections.title: The Kav makes only an above and a below: the teacher's yardstick
sections.summary: The first line is no particular way of drawing down; it only makes that there is an above and a below, a giver and a receiver. Like a teacher hired before he has a student, or a yardstick that measures everything, it holds every length, breadth and height, up to the Essence itself.

phrases.he: להיות ידוע שהקו,
הגם שהוא בא בבחינת המשכה והתפשטות מלמעלה למטה,
אבל אינו ענין פרטית אופן המשכה כלל
רק מה שנמשך האור מלמעלה למטה בלבד
phrases.en: the line is only what is from up to down

phrases.he: שעל ידי זה נמצא בחינת מעלה ומטה מהמשפיע אל המקבל
phrases.en: through this comes a *maala mata* from *mashpia* to the *mekabel*

blocks.text: That's why in general the actual *inyan* of the *kav hamida* is *davka* the *kav katzar*: usually the *kav hamida* means the actual *kav katzar*, which measures everything else. But Rabbi Markel thinks you could also say (he says he hasn't seen it) that the *midida*, the actual measurement, is also the *Kav*. That's why it says that the *Kav* goes down to the end of *Atzilus*: that is its measurement.

blocks.title: The teacher who is going to teach mathematics
blocks.text:
Here he gives a whole fantastic *mashal*, but he gives only the point of it. In a teacher, as was said before, there is a whole original *Or Ein Sof* of all his knowledge. When he decides what he is going to teach, it all goes into a *tzimtzum*. What is he going to teach? "Mathematics." And to him this one word holds it all. If I tell somebody "I'm going to teach you the *Kav*," I already know, when I say *Kav*, the whole thing I'm going to give over. But to somebody who doesn't know the *inyan* yet, a student, a *mekabel*, it will mean nothing if you tell him *tzimtzum* or *reshimu*, or *Zeir Anpin*. The teacher has in this point the whole entire thing.

Then, in order to teach, he has to think who he is going to teach it to: mathematics to kindergarten kids, to high school kids, or to postgraduate mathematics students. It's all mathematics, all included in the point, but the *Kav* will have to come out different.

Now, this is not the *kav katzar*. It is the *Kav* between the *mashpia* (giver) and the *mekabel*, the actual measurement, and that is also called the *Kav*: a line between two points, one point the *mashpia* and the other the *mekabel*. That is the length of the line, what chapter one calls the *orech* (length): the *orech* of *bina* is the length of the explanation between the *mashpia* and the *mekabel*. But it is not the *kav katzar*.

The *kav hamida* means there is no *mekabel* yet. They just told him he's going to teach; they hired him as a teacher. So there is a *hiyuli* ability within himself to measure whoever it is, and to measure all kinds of lines. Later he is going to explain that this is like a tape measure ("A yardstick," a student puts in; like a yardstick, right), the tape measure a craftsman uses.

blocks.title: Measuring your house with a ten-foot tape
blocks.text: "Let's measure your house." "Well, how am I going to measure it?" "Here, I got a measuring tape. It's ten feet long, a ten-foot measuring tape." "Wait a minute, my house is more than ten feet long. How are you going to measure all the things, the length of the house?" "Well, I want to measure everything: the length of the house, the length of the windows and the height of the windows, the depth of the room and the height of the room, and the yard. We're going to measure everything, and from this we'll be able to make a blueprint of your house and give a full description of it." "Wait a minute, ten feet is not enough." "No, it's enough. Even if I had one inch it's enough. That's all you have to have."

blocks.title: Measuring by krypton
blocks.text: As a matter of fact, the way the scientists measure now, the accurate measurements they have of a centimeter and so on, is by the wavelength of krypton. Krypton is a gas, like neon. A krypton lamp puts out a sort of greenish light, and it has a specific wavelength, something like a millionth of an inch. And yet everything is measured by this thing that's a millionth of an inch. Why? Because once you have any exact measurement, you can measure all the measurements with it.

With a yardstick you can measure the distance from here to the moon. The same with the *kav hamida* inside the teacher: it measures the distance between the *mashpia* and the *mekabel*, of any *mekabel*, as a student says.

It could be a *mekabel* who is *mamash* the same as him, and then all you need to give it over is a *kav katzar*; or a little bit longer, down to *Adam Kadmon*, or down to *Atzilus*, or all the way down to us, to *Asiya*, or even all the way down to creatures that are almost like monkeys. You can measure any kind of line with it.

sensitivity.reason: Describes the lowest possible receivers as "creatures that are almost like monkeys".
sensitivity.publishable: It could be a *mekabel* who is *mamash* the same as him, and then all you need to give it over is a *kav katzar*; or a little bit longer, down to *Adam Kadmon*, or down to *Atzilus*, or all the way down to us, to *Asiya*, or even further down. You can measure any kind of line with it.

blocks.text: Not only that: this *Kav* of the teacher is a *hiyuli* for all the explanations, because the *orech* of all the explanations comes from it. It is the *Kav* that measures the length, the *orech* of *bina*, from up to down, so it contains all possible explanations within itself. And since it contains not only all the lengths of explanation but all the types of explanation, it also contains all the *rochav* (breadths). With this line you can measure the breadth too.

blocks.title: Square feet out of a yardstick
blocks.text: With a measuring stick I can measure not only the length of your living room but its width too, and the height, and tell you what the *shetach* (area) is. You say, "Wait a minute, how can you get a *shetach* out of a line? The yardstick does not have square feet in it. It only has long feet in it." And yet you can measure the height too, and get volumes out of it. You can measure everything, all the things that were said in chapter one, including the height. And since the height is included in this line, the line can go even higher than itself.

So the line can go backwards. With a measuring stick you can measure not only the positive distance; you can measure the negative distance. Not from one wall to the other wall, but from the wall to the outside of the house: how far away are you from the house altogether? That's just by turning the line around: instead of measuring to the east, you measure to the west. So this line can really measure all the way up to the *Atzmus*.

And really it is a part of the *Atzmus*. Not only that: in this line is included everything that is in the *reshimu*, so he can explain anything. Not only from here down: he can explain the original stuff, the whole *Or Ein Sof*, which is included in this line, and even higher than the *Or Ein Sof*, since, as was said, there is higher than the *Or Ein Sof*. That is really what the explanation of *bina* is about.

So the line is only from up to down, and through it comes an above and a below, from the *mashpia* (giver) to the *mekabel* (receiver). But in the original line there is no actual *mekabel*; he only knows that there is a *mekabel*. That means only that there is an up and a down, nothing more. You don't know where the down is, and therefore you also don't know where the up is. The up doesn't start at the beginning of the line; it starts before the *tzimtzum*, because you don't know how far up into the original *sechel* (intellect) you will have to go to bring it down, since you don't know who you're giving it to. It's just that there is an up and there is a down; that's all it is.

phrases.he: מה שאין כן בהיולי דנקודה
אין בו מעלה ומטה,
phrases.en: there is no up and down

phrases.he: ראש תוך וסוף כו' כידוע
phrases.en: there's no beginning or end, there's no middle

phrases.he: (וזהו מה שכתוב בעץ חיים
דכל עיקר הארת הקו אינו רק להיות בחינת מעלה ומטה כמו שיתבאר)
phrases.en: the whole thing of the *Kav* is only to make up and down

blocks.text: The point is like when you say "mathematics." Which mathematics? The calculus? No, it's just a point. There is no up and down, no beginning or end, no middle: *kulo k'echad*, all of it as one. And that is what *Etz Chaim* says: the whole thing of the *Kav* is only to make up and down. That is the whole *inyan* of the *Kav*.

sections.title: The builder's measuring stick, and the lines of the letter beis
sections.summary: The builder's measure is not part of the building's area, yet it measures every length and breadth. So the *Kav* is the *hiyuli* of the letters, which are made of lines, and through them of every idea.

phrases.he: וכמשל אמת הבנין,
phrases.en: like the measuring stick

phrases.he: שאינו בא בגדר שטח הבנין עצמו,
לאורך ורוחב
רק שבו מודד כל מדידת אורך וכל מדידת רוחב
והוא עצמו רק כמו קו הקצר שכולל כל אופני מדידות של אורך ורוחב כו'

blocks.title: The builder's measuring stick
blocks.text: The *amas habinyan* (the builder's measure) is like the measuring stick. Even for the length, you don't need a different length to measure two feet and a different length to measure fifty feet. You use the same tape measure.
And by the way, the reason physical geometry is like that is because it comes out of this. These *inyanim* are included in the *Kav*; that's why a physical line came out like that.

phrases.he: כך ציור הקו בחינת היולי לגבי בחינת שטח האותיות
phrases.en: Not only that, the *Kav* is also a *hiyuli* for letters.

phrases.he: לעשותם באורך ורוחב,
כמו בחינת קוין שבאות הב' כו'
וכמו שכתוב במקום אחר

blocks.text: Not only that: the *Kav* is also a *hiyuli* for letters. A *beis* is made of three lines: you have three lines, you have a *beis*. If somebody knows how to make a line, you can teach him how to make a *beis*. So this line includes all ideas in it, because it includes all the letters, and the letters can be put into all kinds of ideas.

sections.title: The kav hamida: the whole point, drawn down to the measure of the receivers
sections.summary: The first drawing down of the *Kav* is still a *hiyuli*: nothing has happened yet but "I'm going to teach it to somebody". It holds everything hidden in the point, from the power before the *tzimtzum*, and it comes only to the measure of the receivers; so it is the *hiyuli* of every light and flow they will get.

phrases.he: ולפי זה גם ראשית המשכת הקו מן הנקודה,
הגם שהוא בא בבחינת התפשטות והמשכה,
אבל הוא בחינת המשכה היולית עדיין,
לכלול כמה פרטי אופני המשכות
phrases.en: and this includes all kinds of different *hamshachos*

phrases.he: לאורך ורוחב במדה
ולזה נקרא קו המדה כידוע
phrases.en: and that's why it's called *kav hamida*

phrases.he: ועל זה מורה צורתו שהוא קצר בעצם,
phrases.en: means it just comes out

phrases.he: והולך ונמשך מלמעלה למטה בלבד

blocks.text: It's not that it actually comes out at all. Nothing happened. He just first thought what he's going to teach, mathematics, and then he thought, "Well, I'm going to teach it to somebody." That's it; that's all it is, and that's the line. It includes all kinds of different ways of drawing down, because it's to any somebody. A big somebody, you'll have a big *rochav* that you can give over to him. A little somebody, you won't be able to give him such a big *rochav*, but you'll have to go through a much bigger *orech*.
And that's why it is called *kav hamida*. It just comes out, and that's it.

phrases.he: אבל הוא כולל בהמשכתו על כל פנים כל מה שיש בהעלם ההיולי דנקודה כו',
phrases.en: but it includes in this that it's *mamshich* everything that is hidden in the *reshimu*

phrases.he: רק שבא באופן המשכה למטה
phrases.en: but it comes in a way of spreading downwards

phrases.he: והוא בא מכח אור העצמי הנעלם שבעצמות המשפיע שלפני צמצומו בנקודה א'
phrases.en: and really it comes from the same power that the *tzimtzum* comes

phrases.he: רק שבא דרך קו לבד,
phrases.en: except that it doesn't come in a way of a full infinite light, but only in a way of a *kav katzar*

phrases.he: ולא כמו שהוא בעצמות המשפיע, שהוא בהרחבת הערך של העצמות ממש
phrases.en: the explanation is going to come according to the *mekabel*, not according to how the *mashpia* understands it

blocks.text: It includes in its drawing down everything that is hidden in the *reshimu*, only that it comes in a way of spreading downward. And really it comes from the same power that the *tzimtzum* comes from.

Except that it doesn't come in a way of a full infinite light, but only in a way of a *kav katzar*. In other words, the explanation is going to come according to the *mekabel*, not according to how the *mashpia* understands it.

phrases.he: ובקו זה הנה אור העצמות
בא לפי ערך המקבלים לבד
phrases.en: only according to the students

phrases.he: אבל עם כל זה
הרי יש בו מעין ודוגמת אור העצמות הנעלם בנקודה כו',
phrases.en: It has *mamash*, actually, the same thing like the *or ha'Atzmus* which is in the *reshimu*

phrases.he: רק שבא בדרך המשכה למטה
phrases.en: only that it comes in a way of spreading downwards

phrases.he: על כן בא בציור קו
phrases.en: that's why it comes, and we call it like a line

phrases.he: והוא בחינת היולי לכל אור ושפע המקבלים כו' ודי למבין:
phrases.en: And it's already in a way of a *hiyuli* for any kind of *or* and *shefa* to any kind of *mekabel*, and this is enough to understand.

blocks.text: It comes only according to the *mekablim* (receivers), only according to the students. But nonetheless: this book we are learning now, even though the book is according to us, really comes from the original *harchava* (breadth) of the *Atzmus* of the Rebbe, even when it is in a *Kav*.

It has *mamash* the same thing as the light of the *Atzmus* that is in the *reshimu*, **only that it comes in a way of spreading downward**. That's why it comes as, and we call it, a line. And it is already a *hiyuli* for any kind of light and *shefa* to any kind of *mekabel*. And this is enough to understand.

reviewQuestions.question: In what way does the *Kav* seem to be the opposite of the *reshimu*, and why could the point's being only a point also be the source of revelation?
What does the songwriter's talent, or the soul's power of movement, show about why a *hiyuli* does not spread?
How does the student swallowing his teacher's words show that the *reshimu* is the source of the *Kav*?
What is the *kav katzar*, and why is it still called *stima d'chol stimin*?
Why does the teacher's *kav hamida* exist before he has any student, and how can one yardstick measure a house, its area and even the distance back up to the Essence?
If the line includes everything hidden in the point, in what sense does it still come "only according to the measure of the receivers"?

notes.text: He says "geometry comes from gematria". The usual derivation is the reverse (gematria from the Greek geometria); left as he said it.

Krypton digression: he says the krypton lamp's light is greenish and its wavelength "like a millionth of an inch or something like that". The krypton-86 line that defined the metre (1960-1983) is orange-red, about 606 nm (roughly 1/42,000 inch); left as he said it.
The chicken and vulture remark ("that's how a vulture can tell") is loosely argued in the recording; written as he said it, without tidying the logic.

Class 010 starts on line 33 ("amnam, ma shenimshach bivchinas kav katzar", w3679) before the tape is flipped; class 011 resumes on the kav katzar and rereads the line at w400. Both are under the passage of line 33.

Class 011 w199-266: an exchange about why *Adam Kadmon* is called the *Kav*; the speakers are not labelled. The block keeps it as dialogue, taking the quoted lines as a student's and the rest ("I don't think", "Whatever, but the basic thing...") as his.
Class 010 w3837-3872 ("Yeah, but it's not just that. I'm talking about the level of power") may answer a student's remark; no question is audible, so it is kept inside the explanation.
"This book ... comes from the original harchava of the Atzmus of the Rebbe": "the Rebbe" here is the author of the book.
Line 35: he reads line 35 as "rak shema shenimshach hu inyan maala umata bilvad", not the printed text; the phrase is the printed text rendered plainly.
Class 010 w3093-3133: he says "like we explained, like the Gemara in the Mishna"; the reference is unclear as spoken and is kept as he said it.
